verses.text: These are the stages of the journey of the people of Israel, when they came out of Egypt in their army groups, led by Moses and Aaron.
At the LORD's command, Moses wrote down the places where they started each stage of their journey. These are the stages, from one starting place to the next.
The people of Israel set out from Rameses on the fifteenth day of the first month, the day after the Passover. They marched out boldly while all the Egyptians watched,
as the Egyptians were burying all their firstborn sons, whom the LORD had struck down. The LORD had also judged their gods.
The people of Israel left Rameses and camped at Succoth.
They left Succoth and camped at Etham, at the edge of the desert.
They left Etham, turned back to Pi Hahiroth, east of Baal Zephon, and camped near Migdol.
They left Pi Hahiroth and walked through the middle of the sea into the desert. After travelling three days in the desert of Etham, they camped at Marah.
They left Marah and came to Elim, where there were twelve springs of water and seventy palm trees. They camped there.
They left Elim and camped by the Red Sea.
They left the Red Sea and camped in the desert of Sin.
They left the desert of Sin and camped at Dophkah.
They left Dophkah and camped at Alush.
They left Alush and camped at Rephidim, where there was no water for the people to drink.
They left Rephidim and camped in the Sinai desert.
They left the Sinai desert and camped at Kibroth Hattaavah.
They left Kibroth Hattaavah and camped at Hazeroth.
They left Hazeroth and camped at Rithmah.
They left Rithmah and camped at Rimmon Perez.
They left Rimmon Perez and camped at Libnah.
They left Libnah and camped at Rissah.
They left Rissah and camped at Kehelathah.
They left Kehelathah and camped at Mount Shepher.
They left Mount Shepher and camped at Haradah.
They left Haradah and camped at Makheloth.
They left Makheloth and camped at Tahath.
They left Tahath and camped at Terah.
They left Terah and camped at Mithkah.
They left Mithkah and camped at Hashmonah.
They left Hashmonah and camped at Moseroth.
They left Moseroth and camped at Bene Jaakan.
They left Bene Jaakan and camped at Hor Haggidgad.
They left Hor Haggidgad and camped at Jotbathah.
They left Jotbathah and camped at Abronah.
They left Abronah and camped at Ezion Geber.
They left Ezion Geber and camped at Kadesh, in the desert of Zin.
They left Kadesh and camped at Mount Hor, on the edge of the land of Edom.
At the LORD's command, Aaron the priest went up Mount Hor, and he died there on the first day of the fifth month, in the fortieth year after the people of Israel came out of Egypt.
Aaron was one hundred twenty-three years old when he died on Mount Hor.
The Canaanite king of Arad, who lived in the Negev in the land of Canaan, heard that the people of Israel were coming.
They left Mount Hor and camped at Zalmonah.
They left Zalmonah and camped at Punon.
They left Punon and camped at Oboth.
They left Oboth and camped at Iye Abarim, on the border of Moab.
They left Iyim and camped at Dibon Gad.
They left Dibon Gad and camped at Almon Diblathaim.
They left Almon Diblathaim and camped in the Abarim mountains, near Nebo.
They left the Abarim mountains and camped on the plains of Moab, beside the Jordan River across from Jericho.
There on the plains of Moab they camped along the Jordan, from Beth Jeshimoth to Abel Shittim.
On the plains of Moab, beside the Jordan across from Jericho, the LORD said to Moses,
"Speak to the people of Israel and tell them: When you cross the Jordan into the land of Canaan,
you must drive out all the people who live in the land ahead of you. Destroy all their carved stone idols and their metal statues, and tear down all their places of worship on the hills.
Take over the land and settle in it, for I have given you the land to own.

Divide the land among your clans by casting lots. Give a larger share to a larger clan and a smaller share to a smaller clan. Whatever land the lot falls on for each clan will be theirs. Divide it among your ancestral tribes.

But if you do not drive out the people who live in the land, those you allow to stay will be like splinters in your eyes and thorns in your sides. They will cause you trouble in the land where you live.
And then I will do to you what I planned to do to them."
